They fished all night and caught nothing. Then Jesus said: try again. 🎣 Luke 5:1-11

Peter was tired, empty-handed, and honest: “Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net” (Luke 5:5). The net broke. Two boats began to sink. And Jesus said, “Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.”

What's your “nevertheless” this week? 👇

The whole mountain shook when God came down. 🔥 Exodus 19-20

Thunder, lightning, a thick cloud, a trumpet louder and louder, and “mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the Lord descended upon it in fire” (Exodus 19:18). Then God spoke. And notice how He started: “I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt” (Exodus 20:2). Rescue first. Then the commandments.

How many of the Ten Commandments can you name from memory? 👇

Bible Quiz #7. Only true Bible nerds get 3/3. 🧠

Three questions: how many languages the earth spoke before Babel (Genesis 11), when Nicodemus came to see Jesus (John 3), and how many times Naaman dipped in the Jordan (2 Kings 5). Answer before you swipe, no Googling.

5,000 men. 5 loaves. 2 small fish. 🍞 John 6:1-14

Philip did the math and it didn't work. Andrew found a boy with “five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?” (John 6:9). Jesus gave thanks, everyone ate as much as they wanted, and they gathered twelve baskets of leftovers.

What's the “little” you can put in His hands today? 👇

God told him: you have TOO MANY soldiers. 🎺 Judges 6-7

Gideon was hiding when the angel called him “thou mighty man of valour” (Judges 6:12). Thirty-two thousand men became ten thousand, then three hundred. Trumpets, jars, torches, one shout, and the whole enemy army ran. Why so few? “Lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me” (Judges 7:2).

Where do you feel like “the least” right now? 👇
